metaDescription: Soundbars under $500 compared by Atmos height speakers, wireless subwoofer size, Wi-Fi streaming and voice assistants, with honest notes on room fit and setup.
expertTake: The JBL BAR-500-MK2 is the best overall pick because it pairs Dolby Atmos with a 10 inch wireless subwoofer and MultiBeam processing. The Sony BRAVIA Theater Bar 6 is the best value for a 3.1.2 layout with up-firing speakers. Skip Atmos bars in rooms with high, sloped or very low ceilings, because up-firing speakers need a flat ceiling to bounce sound off.
introParagraphs: At the upper end of a modest budget, a soundbar stops being a slim speaker and becomes a small home theater: it adds up-firing speakers for height, a bigger subwoofer, Wi-Fi streaming and voice assistants. The question is which of these extras you will actually use, and how your room treats them.

The cap reflects listing prices on the day we updated the guide, and prices move often. We kept this lineup distinct from our lower cap soundbar guides by favouring bars with up-firing speakers, larger subwoofers or streaming features. We have not handled any of these bars, so our judgments rest on specifications and patterns in owner feedback, including how up-firing and wireless systems behave in real rooms.

products.name: JBL BAR-500-MK2 Dolby Atmos Soundbar with 10 inch Wireless Subwoofer, MultiBeam 3.0

specList.label: Listing note
specList.value: Sold with a protection plan bundle

products.description:
This is the newest JBL in the group, pairing Dolby Atmos with a 10 inch wireless subwoofer and MultiBeam 3.0 processing that bounces sound off walls to fill the room. The maker's SmartDetails processing is described as restoring fine detail in dialogue and effects. A 10 inch subwoofer is larger than the sub on most bars at this cap and moves more air for bass.

The tradeoff is that the listing is a bundle that includes a protection plan, so read the title carefully, and that MultiBeam depends on your walls, so a room with an open side will lose some effect. Compared with the JBL Bar 500, the MK2 has a stated 10 inch sub and an updated processing label. Large subwoofers need space and can overpower a small room.

Place the bar centred under the TV and the sub a few inches from a wall. Run the room calibration if the bar offers one. Set the bass to a level your neighbours can accept.
products.bestFor: A medium to large living room with walls that can reflect sound.
pros: 10 inch wireless subwoofer delivers real bass
Dolby Atmos and MultiBeam 3.0 widen the soundstage
SmartDetails processing is listed for dialogue and effects
Bar and sub from a brand with a large support network
cons: A large subwoofer can overpower a small room

products.name: JBL Bar 500 5.1 Channel Soundbar with MultiBeam, Dolby Atmos, Wi-Fi, AirPlay, Chromecast, 590 W
products.description:
This 5.1 channel bar combines Dolby Atmos and MultiBeam surround with built-in Wi-Fi, AirPlay, Alexa multi-room music and Chromecast, rated at 590 watts total system output. The streaming features make it a music system as well as a TV bar, and it can join a multi-room setup. Atmos support with a wireless sub adds a movie-friendly spec sheet.

The compromise is that 590 watts is a peak system number, and the bar is the previous generation of the BAR-500 line. Compared with the MK2, it lists streaming features and a higher watt figure, but fewer details on the subwoofer in the compact data. A Wi-Fi bar can need firmware updates and a stable network.

Put the bar and TV on the same Wi-Fi network and name them clearly in the app. Test AirPlay and Chromecast in the return window. Update the firmware when asked.
products.bestFor: A shopper who wants a movie bar that also streams music around the home.
pros: Wi-Fi, AirPlay, Alexa multi-room and Chromecast are listed
5.1 channels with Dolby Atmos and MultiBeam
590 W total system output is stated
Works as a music system as well as a TV bar
cons: Previous generation of the BAR-500 line

products.name: Sony BRAVIA Theater Bar 6 3.1.2 Channel Soundbar with Wireless Subwoofer, Dolby Atmos, DTS:X
products.description:
This is a 3.1.2 channel bar with three front-firing speakers, two up-firing speakers, a wireless subwoofer and support for Dolby Atmos and DTS:X. The dedicated centre channel supports clear dialogue, and the two up-firing speakers add real height cues by bouncing sound off the ceiling. Few bars at this cap list both a centre and up-firing speakers.

The tradeoff is that up-firing speakers need a flat ceiling about 8 to 10 feet high, and sloped or very high ceilings reduce the effect. Compared with the Hisense, the Sony is a more established name, but the compact data does not state wattage. The wireless sub is easy to place but needs an outlet.

Check your ceiling before you buy, and place the bar directly in front of the TV. Run the room calibration if available. Use the voice mode for dialogue.
products.bestFor: A living room with a flat, standard-height ceiling that benefits from up-firing speakers.
pros: 3.1.2 layout includes a dedicated centre and two up-firing speakers
Dolby Atmos and DTS:X are supported
Wireless subwoofer adds bass
Established brand with strong TV integration
cons: Up-firing needs a flat ceiling of normal height
Compact data does not state wattage

products.name: Hisense AX3120Q 3.1.2 Channel Soundbar with 6.5 inch Wireless Subwoofer, Dolby Atmos, DTS:X, Bluetooth 5.3
products.description:
This bar lists five front-firing and two up-firing speakers plus a 6.5 inch wireless subwoofer, with Dolby Atmos, DTS:X, Bluetooth 5.3 and HDMI. Quick touch EQ modes let you switch between music, movies and news from the remote. It offers a similar 3.1.2 layout to the Sony at a lower cost position.

The tradeoff is that the brand is less established as an audio name, and a 6.5 inch sub is smaller than the JBL's 10 inch unit. Compared with the Sony, it lists more front speakers and a stated sub size, but fewer details on processing. Check the warranty and the firmware support.

Place the bar on a flat surface under the TV and keep the up-firing speakers uncovered. Adjust the EQ mode to the content. Keep the sub away from the TV.
products.bestFor: A budget-conscious shopper who wants a 3.1.2 layout with a stated subwoofer size.
pros: 5 front-firing and 2 up-firing speakers are listed
6.5 inch wireless subwoofer is stated
Bluetooth 5.3 for music streaming
Quick EQ modes simplify tuning
cons: Smaller 6.5 inch sub than the JBL's 10 inch

products.name: Bose Smart Dolby Atmos Soundbar with A.I. Dialogue Mode, TrueSpace, Alexa voice control
products.description:
This is a compact all-in-one bar with Dolby Atmos, TrueSpace processing that upmixes non-Atmos content, an A.I. Dialogue Mode and built-in voice control. The listing says an acoustic architecture fits several arrays into a small chassis, which suits a small TV stand. It does not include a subwoofer, and Bose sells a bass module separately.

The tradeoff is that without a subwoofer, bass is limited, and Bose bars cost more per feature than the competition. Compared with the JBL, it is more compact and smarter, but bass is thinner. The compact data does not state wattage or speaker count.

Place it on a TV stand and run the room setup in the Bose app. Add a bass module later if you want more low end. Use the dialogue mode for speech-heavy shows.
products.bestFor: A smaller room where a compact, voice-controlled bar fits better than a big sub.
pros: Dolby Atmos support in a compact bar
A.I. Dialogue Mode targets speech clarity
TrueSpace upmixes non-Atmos content
Built-in voice control
cons: No subwoofer, so bass is limited
Compact data gives no wattage or speaker count

products.name: Bose Soundbar 500 with Alexa and Google Assistant, eight-microphone array, Wi-Fi, AirPlay 2

specList.label: Design
specList.value: Slim, does not block the screen

products.description:
This slim bar includes both Alexa and Google Assistant, an eight-microphone array with noise rejection, and Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and AirPlay 2 streaming. It is designed to sit under a TV without blocking the screen, and it works as a smart speaker as well as a TV bar. It is the older model in the Bose line.

The compromise is that it is a 2.0-style bar with no up-firing speakers, and bass is limited without the separate bass module. Compared with the Bose Smart Dolby Atmos, it is older and lacks Atmos, but it has two assistants. The compact data does not state channels.

Place it centred under the TV and connect by HDMI ARC. Set up the voice assistant you prefer. Add a bass module if you want more low end.

buyingCriteria.explanation: At this cap you can buy up-firing speakers, a larger subwoofer, Wi-Fi streaming, voice assistants and a better-known name. The Sony and Hisense add height, the JBL adds a 10 inch sub, and the Bose models add voice and streaming. Lower cap bars skip these. Check your TV's HDMI ARC or eARC port is free and labelled, since many TVs have only one and it may already be used by another device. Treat a stated peak wattage as a rough size class and not a promise, and judge a bar by how clean it sounds at a normal listening level.

Up-firing speakers bounce sound off the ceiling, and the effect works best with a flat ceiling of about 8 to 10 feet. Sloped, vaulted or very low ceilings reduce it. In those rooms, a 3.1 bar without height may be as good. Measure the depth of your TV stand, because a bar with up-firing speakers should sit on a surface with nothing above it and ideally at least a foot of clearance.

A 10 inch sub, as on the JBL, moves more air than a 6.5 inch sub. Larger subs need space and can overpower a small room. Place it near the front, a few inches from a wall, and not in a corner. Think about the neighbours: a 10 inch subwoofer in an apartment can transmit vibration through the floor, so look for a bass level control and a night mode.

Wi-Fi bars, such as the JBL Bar 500 and Bose Soundbar 500, stream music and join multi-room systems. Voice assistants add convenience and a microphone in your living room. Check that your assistant of choice is supported. Look at the remote and the app, since a bar with excellent speakers and a confusing setup will not be used to its potential.
HDMI ARC or eARC carries audio from the TV, and eARC supports higher quality formats. Check your TV's ports and whether the bar has a pass-through. An optical input limits formats.
A bar with a big sub suits a living room of 200 square feet or more, and a compact bar suits a small room. Apartment living calls for a night mode and a bass control. Think about neighbours.

specDecoder.meaning: Three front channels, one subwoofer and two height channels from up-firing speakers. Height channels need an Atmos track to do their best work, and ordinary stereo content is upmixed by processing.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Sony and Hisense list 3.1.2, and the JBL Bar 500 lists 5.1.

specDecoder.meaning: A driver angled upward to bounce sound off the ceiling for height cues. Up-firing drivers point at about 45 to 70 degrees upward, and a ceiling with texture scatters sound more than a smooth one.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Sony and Hisense list up-firing speakers, and the Bose Atmos bar uses its own arrays.

specDecoder.meaning: JBL's processing that bounces sound beams off walls to create a wider field. Wall reflections matter, so a bar in a room with large windows or open doorways loses some beam width.
specDecoder.watchFor: The JBL bars list MultiBeam, which depends on your wall layout.

specDecoder.meaning: Bose processing that upmixes non-Atmos content to a spatial presentation. Upmixing converts stereo or 5.1 content into a wider presentation, which can be pleasing or artificial depending on taste.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Bose Smart Dolby Atmos bar lists TrueSpace.

specDecoder.meaning: Apple's wireless audio system that streams from iPhones and Macs. Apple devices can send audio directly to the bar without going through the TV, and this works only when both are on the same network.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Bose Soundbar 500 and JBL Bar 500 list AirPlay.

howWeEvaluated.title: Layout and height
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated each bar on the channel layout and speakers stated in its listing. The Sony and Hisense list up-firing speakers. We have not handled any of these bars. We looked for any mention of ceiling height or room size in each listing, because those details decide whether up-firing speakers will do their job.

howWeEvaluated.title: Subwoofer and bass
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared subwoofers. The JBL MK2 lists 10 inches, the Hisense 6.5, and the Bose bars list none. Owner feedback patterns often mention weak or boomy bass. We separated bars that include a subwoofer from those that do not, since bass is the biggest practical difference between them.

howWeEvaluated.title: Streaming and voice
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered Wi-Fi, AirPlay and assistants. The JBL Bar 500 and Bose bars lead. We do not publish ratings or review counts.

howWeEvaluated.title: Distinct from lower caps
howWeEvaluated.description: We avoided repeating our 300 and lower cap lineups and left out renewed units and accessories. We kept bundles only when the soundbar was the product.

howWeEvaluated.title: Honest limits
howWeEvaluated.description: Atmos in a bar is an effect, and a room can help or hurt it. We say so.

maintenance.why: Updates fix connectivity and audio bugs. Check the bar's position every few months, since it can be nudged forward on a stand and block the TV's remote sensor.
Calibration depends on the room. Re-run the setup after you change the layout of the room, particularly after a new sofa or curtains.

maintenance.task: Dust the grille and up-firing drivers
maintenance.why: Dust on up-firing speakers dulls the effect.
Wireless subs sometimes lose their link.
A wrong input causes no sound or poor formats.

faq.q: Do up-firing speakers work in every room?
faq.a: They work best with a flat ceiling of normal height. Sloped or very high ceilings reduce the effect. If the sound lags behind the picture, check the audio delay setting on the TV or the bar. Wall mounting a bar is possible, but check the weight and the keyhole slots before you commit.

faq.q: Is a 10 inch subwoofer too big?
faq.a: For a small room, it can overpower. Use the bass control and place it away from corners. Keep the original box if you rent, because bars are awkward to move without their packaging.

faq.q: Do I need Wi-Fi in a soundbar?
faq.a: Only if you want to stream music or use multi-room features. Bluetooth is enough for basics. A short HDMI cable that meets the right standard is better than a long, cheap one.
A newer HDMI feature that carries higher quality audio from the TV to the bar.
Yes. The cap reflects listing prices when we updated the guide, and prices move often.

faq.q: Is Dolby Atmos worth it on a bar?
faq.a: It adds height cues when the bar has up-firing speakers, and a virtual effect otherwise.
